testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If your vehicle has an inspection report, you should:

options.text: Ignore the report and find any problems yourself.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.
Skip the pre-trip inspection and use only the report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the report.
questions.explanation: Start your vehicle inspection by reading the last inspection report. The repair company should have fixed any problems listed in the report.

questions.question: When carrying a wide load, you should:

options.text: Get special permits and follow special rules, such as driving at certain times.
Honk at other drivers to make them move out of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules, such as driving at certain times.
questions.explanation: Over-sized loads need special permits. They can only be driven on roads at certain times and may need special warning signs or equipment.

questions.question: Poor weight balance in a trailer:
questions.correctAnswerText: Makes handling unsafe.
questions.explanation: Poor weight balance in a trailer is unsafe. Too much or too little weight on the front axle makes steering difficult. Weight should be spread evenly from front to back and side to side, and positioned as low as possible.

questions.question: Hydroplaning:

options.text: Usually happens when driving faster than 65 mph.
Can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose grip on the road and slide on a water layer. You do not need a large amount of water for this to happen. Hydroplaning can start at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: What is road rage?

options.text: Driving with the intent to harm others
Driving a vehicle that is unsafe
Driving a vehicle that has not been inspected

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving with the intent to harm others
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving means driving in a selfish or pushy way. Road rage means driving with the intent to harm others or to physically hurt another driver or their vehicle.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should use your turn signal:

options.text: Only when there is other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always.
questions.explanation: You must always signal properly before turning or changing lanes.

questions.question: Blocking cargo:

options.text: Should be done to stop cargo from moving.
Can only be done with metal pieces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be done to stop cargo from moving.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing keep cargo from moving during transport. Block cargo on its front, back, and sides to prevent movement.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: When stopped at a traffic light

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving
questions.explanation: Check and adjust mirrors before starting each trip. Any trailer should be straight when adjusting mirrors.

questions.question: Emergency brakes are:

options.text: Only required when hauling hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required on tractors.
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, brakes can fade. What does brake fade mean?

options.text: They work differently in front and back.

questions.correctAnswerText: They become less effective.
questions.explanation: Using brakes too much on a steep hill causes them to overheat and stop working as well. To prevent brake overheating on a steep hill, use engine braking instead.

questions.question: Using brakes creates heat. If too much heat builds up:

options.text: The brakes may squeak more than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may not work.
questions.explanation: Brakes can handle a lot of heat, but do not rely only on them to slow your vehicle. If brakes get too hot, they can fade and stop working. Also use engine braking to help slow down.

questions.question: When using a turn signal, you should not:

options.text: Leave the turn signal on long after you finish turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the turn signal on long after you finish turning.
questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn or change lanes. Keep signaling while you turn or change lanes. Turn off the signal once you finish so other drivers do not get confused.

questions.question: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) does not need to include which of the following?

options.text: Number of meals the driver ate

questions.correctAnswerText: Number of meals the driver ate
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include distance traveled and fuel purchased. It must show where the trip started and ended, and list the Vehicle Identification Number. It does not need to include what the driver ate.

questions.question: The suspension system:

options.text: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
Keeps the load the proper distance behind the driver's compartment.
Maintains a safe distance between the vehicle and other vehicles.
Lightens the load for the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports the vehicle and its load while keeping the axles in place. Problems with the suspension system are very dangerous.

questions.question: Looking far ahead of your vehicle while driving is:

options.text: Discouraged, as there is little you can do about something far up the road.
Encouraged so you can spot hazards early.
Only encouraged if you are carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encouraged so you can spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to spot hazards early and react safely.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, what is the maximum leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes?
questions.correctAnswerText: 3 psi in one minute
questions.explanation: Know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A single vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than 3 psi in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Is common if a vehicle is warmed up.
Is encouraged to improve gas mileage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can damage a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough, jerky acceleration can damage the vehicle.

questions.question: What is the best advice for driving in fog?

options.text: Avoid driving in fog if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving in fog if possible.
questions.explanation: Fog makes driving very dangerous. Avoid it if you can. If you must drive in fog, use low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the day.

questions.question: If you pull over to the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Allow your taillights to alert other motorists.
Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other motorists.
Keep your lights off to avoid distracting other motorists.
Keep your door open to warn other motorists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other motorists.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers when you stop on the side of the road. This is especially important at night. Taillights alone are not enough because other drivers might think you are moving normally and hit you.

questions.question: Improperly loaded cargo can:

options.text: Hurt or kill the driver during a sudden stop.
Make it easier to stop a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hurt or kill the driver during a sudden stop.
questions.explanation: Unsecured cargo is very dangerous. If you stop suddenly, loose cargo can fall and injure or kill the driver.

questions.question: You must always be able to stop within:

options.text: The distance you can see ahead on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you can see ahead on the road.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must be able to stop within the area you can see. You must slow down when visibility is poor.

questions.question: Driving at night is:

options.text: Safer than driving during the day.
Just as safe as driving during the day.
More dangerous than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. It is harder to see hazards. Headlight glare affects vision. There are more tired and impaired drivers on the road.

questions.question: If wheel bearing seals are leaking, you should:

options.text: Add more grease until the seal is full.
Add brake fluid to the bearing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get the seals repaired.
questions.explanation: Check wheel bearing seals during vehicle inspection. If you find any unsafe part, get it fixed. Federal and state laws require that all vehicles be safe to operate.

questions.question: What is another name for front-end header boards?
questions.correctAnswerText: Headache racks
questions.explanation: Front-end header boards are also called "headache racks." They protect the driver from cargo that moves during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of drowsiness?
questions.correctAnswerText: Feeling hungry
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving is dangerous and must be avoided. Signs of drowsiness include frequent blinking, eyes closing or losing focus, yawning, and drifting between lanes.

questions.question: While driving:

options.text: You do not need to tell others your intentions.
You should only use turn signals if a vehicle is next to you.
You should not use a turn signal if the lane change will be obvious.
You should always use turn signals to tell others your intentions.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should always use turn signals to tell others your intentions.
questions.explanation: Always use proper signals to let other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.question: If you are being tailgated while driving a large vehicle, do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your distance from the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: If being tailgated, slow down gradually and increase your distance from the vehicle ahead. Do not speed up—the other driver will just tailgate you faster. Do not use your taillights or brake lights to signal the other driver.

questions.question: When inspecting the exhaust system, which is NOT a problem?

options.text: Exhaust parts not touching fuel system parts

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust parts not touching fuel system parts
questions.explanation: Watch for loose, broken, or missing exhaust pipes and parts. Check for loose or broken mounting brackets. Look for exhaust parts that rub against fuel system parts or other vehicle parts. Check for leaks in the exhaust system.

questions.question: When driving through a curve on the skills test, you should:

options.text: Leave your lane if needed to complete the curve.
Slow down after entering the curve.
Stop checking for other vehicles while turning.
Slow down before entering the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve so you do not need to brake in the curve. Stay in your lane and keep checking for traffic in all directions.

questions.question: When doing an offset back/left parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Move forward straight, then back up to the left.
Back up straight, then move forward to the left.
Move forward straight, then back up straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward straight, then back up to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, move forward straight first, then back up to the left. Your vehicle must be parked completely within the parking space lines.

questions.question: What happens if you don't pass the air brakes endorsement test?

options.text: You cannot drive a vehicle with air brakes.
Your CDL will have an air brake endorsement marked with an asterisk.
Your CDL will not be valid.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot drive a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: If you do not pass the air brakes test, you will not be allowed to drive vehicles with air brakes.

questions.question: What happens when a vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: The tires lose contact with the road.
The trailer separates from the tractor.
The vehicle becomes easier to control.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires lose contact with the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose grip on a wet road and slide on water. The tires glide on the water instead of gripping the road. This can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure in the air tanks drops below 60 psi?

options.text: The vehicle will not shift out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: A warning light turns on.
questions.explanation: When air pressure drops below 60 psi, a low pressure warning signal activates. This signal appears as a warning light or a wig wag.

questions.question: Which of the following shows you are drowsy while driving?

options.text: Your eyes go out of focus on their own
You have trouble holding your head up
You drift from lane to lane

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Signs of drowsiness include eyes closing or losing focus, trouble keeping your head up, and drifting between lanes.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Quickly swerve into the other lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors and use your signal when changing lanes. Make sure there is enough space for your whole vehicle in the next lane before you move.

questions.question: Which of the following surfaces is the most slippery?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wet ice
questions.explanation: Wet ice forms when it is warm enough to melt the ice slightly. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness before a long trip?

options.text: Get about four hours of sleep.
Plan rest stops into your trip ahead of time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan rest stops into your trip ahead of time.
questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness on a long trip, get enough sleep beforehand, plan your route and rest stops in advance, drive with a passenger, and drive during times when you are normally awake.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, a CDL applicant may be asked to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Check the engine oil level.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you may need to check the engine oil level in the engine compartment.

questions.question: Bracing is used to:

options.text: Make items stand taller in a trailer.
Stop items from moving in a trailer.
Make it easier to unload items from a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop items from moving in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing prevent cargo from shifting during transport. Blocking is placed in front, back, and on the sides of cargo. Bracing reaches from the top of the cargo to the floor and sides of the trailer.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Makes a loud squeaking noise when used.
Helps you stay in control while braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you stay in control while braking.
questions.explanation: ABS gives you better control when braking. It does not necessarily change how far your vehicle needs to stop.

questions.question: When slowing down, you should ____ to warn other drivers
questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brakes
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brakes when slowing down. This makes your brake lights flash. Drivers behind you will see this warning.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts:

options.text: Should be repaired, but do not need to be repaired immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are extremely dangerous.
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up your vehicle and keeps the axles in place. Broken parts like springs, shock absorbers, or frame members are very dangerous. Check your vehicle regularly for damage.

questions.question: If you realize you may be running late to your destination, you should:

options.text: Drive while using flashing lights so other road users move out of your path.
Drive at a safe speed and arrive when you arrive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a safe speed and arrive when you arrive.
questions.explanation: Do not drive dangerously or aggressively if you are late. Stay calm and accept delays. Plan extra time for your trips to avoid stress.

questions.question: A vehicle that is smaller than your vehicle:

options.text: Will usually be able to stop faster than your vehicle.
Will usually take more time to stop than your vehicle.
Will take about the same amount of time to stop as your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will usually be able to stop faster than your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Smaller vehicles usually stop faster than larger vehicles. Remember this when deciding how far back to follow other cars.

questions.question: When approaching an active railroad crossing:

options.text: You should expect to hear any approaching train.
You may not hear a train as it approaches.
You will hear two short blasts of the train's horn.
There will always be flashing warning lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not hear a train as it approaches.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on hearing a train. Trains may be quiet in some areas, or your vehicle's noise may cover the sound. Do not assume warning lights will always be there.

questions.question: When inspecting your brakes, a slack adjuster should move ____ from where it is attached to the push rod.
questions.correctAnswerText: No more than one inch
questions.explanation: Pull each slack adjuster to check it. It should not move more than about one inch. If it moves more than one inch, it needs to be adjusted or fixed.

questions.question: When checking your tires as part of the pre-trip inspection, you should look at the:
questions.correctAnswerText: Tire pressure.
questions.explanation: Check that tire pressure is correct. It should not be too low or too high.

questions.question: While operating a CMV:

options.text: You are not required to wear a safety belt.
You are only required to wear a safety belt if your vehicle does not have airbags.
You are required to wear a safety belt, but only if hauling more than 1,000 pounds of cargo.
You are always required to wear a safety belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are always required to wear a safety belt.
questions.explanation: Always wear a safety belt when driving. It is your best protection in a crash.

questions.question: To make your vehicle more visible during the day, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights during the day for best visibility. Do not use high beams around other drivers.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a reason to use your mirrors?

options.text: You are looking at fuel prices.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are looking at fuel prices.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly when turning, changing lanes, merging, and making tight moves. Do not use mirrors to look at fuel prices.
